results.title: DAEODON: The Bone-Crushing Giant That Ruled Ancient... - YouTube
results.snippet: Meet Daeodon shoshonensis, one of the largest and best-known entelodonts ever discovered. Often given dramatic nicknames such as “Hell Pig,” Daeodon was not actually a pig.

results.title: Evidence of Neanderthal Cannibalism Puzzles Researchers
results.snippet: The team has uncovered evidence of cannibalism among a population of Neanderthals at the Goyet cave site in Belgium—the first discovery of Neanderthal cannibalism in Northern Europe.

results.title: Evidence unearthed of possible mass cannibalism in Neolithic Europe
results.snippet: Evidence of cannibalism in Neolithic Europe is rare, but hundreds of remains excavated at a site near the village of Herxheim have markings suggestive of cannibalism.

results.title: The Archaeology of Cannibalism: a Review of the Taphonomic Traits...
results.snippet: The central question surrounding fragmented, modified human assemblages is whether the bone evidence is the result of natural modifications, funerary behaviour or cannibalism.
